base_authority: Original v048 full working tree is preserved unchanged under 00-06/90/95/96/98/99. All post-v048 work is carried under 97_CONTINUATION_MASTER_2026-08-30.
load_rule: Load base authority first, then overlays strictly in master_load_order. Later correction/re-audit overlays supersede contradictory earlier working propositions without deleting provenance.
critical_supersession_guards: Historical Operation SA No.1 three-heavy-cruiser sortie is cancelled in this branch; Tone/Chikuma remain tied to mobile-fleet requirements unless later re-released.
Yamamoto Isoroku survives 1943-04-18 and remains Combined Fleet commander through the current frontier; do not instantiate the historical Koga->Toyoda command chain.
Eastern Fleet / Bay of Bengal is backgrounded after the spring mutual-preservation sequence unless a new land/sea trigger reopens it.
Ichigo-equivalent Hunan main offensive is branch-reconstructed: staff study 1943 late; logistics gates close 1944-04-26; attack begins 1944-04-28. Old 5/10 or 5/27 future clocks are non-controlling.
Old Marianas settlement is reopened. Use current 16-fast-deck US TF58 branch OOB, current Japanese carrier/aircrew recovery, no KON/Biak diversion, Yamamoto command, and current armor ledger.
A7M combat credit is zero at current frontier. Do not introduce Reppu into Marianas combat.
Japanese five-carrier first-line strike system and six secondary carriers remain separate capability ledgers; do not sum them as a homogeneous strike package.
US submarine contacts provide operational/strategic track, not continuous weapon-quality shadowing; Japanese ASW/COMSEC improvements affect persistence, not US submarine existence.

current_state_summary.US: Saipan D-Day lodgment established 15 Jun; TF58 retains 16 fast decks, with about 12 kept in Saipan/Philippine-Sea protection and one ~4-deck Bonins suppression group under early-return logic. US submarines confirm a major Japanese carrier-battleship sortie but do not maintain continuous attack-quality shadowing.
current_state_summary.Japan_mobile: Five first-line carriers remain about 356-379 mission-ready aircraft; six secondary carriers about 143-179 combat-usable aircraft; seven battleships remain available in the battle system. Main force is roughly 700-850 nmi WSW of Saipan late 15 Jun, searching rather than launching a blind maximum-range strike.
current_state_summary.Japan_Marianas_air: Local air has been reduced to about 58-78 onsite ready aircraft by end 15 Jun; still capable of reconnaissance and small strikes, not theater air superiority.
current_state_summary.Saipan_ground: US beachhead survives but is shallow/disorganized; Japanese 9th Tank Regiment opens with the re-audited 57-64 ready armored vehicles and preserves much of its strength through packet tactics. Regiment-scale 16/17 Jun mass-counterattack gate remains open.
current_state_summary.China: Hunan offensive began 28 Apr; Changsha node transferred and partially operational under Japan/Nanjing administration; Hengyang airfield physical control shifted to Japan but Hengyang city/rail/C2 node remains Chinese at the last detailed China state and is backgrounded during Marianas focus unless a trigger fires.
current_state_summary.technology: Seiran I-400/I-401 6-aircraft raid executed against Majuro 3 Jun with limited logistics disruption; I-34 returned Singapore 12 Jun with high-density technical documents/small hardware, while full Jumo/HWK hardware remains an I-29 gate. Reppu remains prototype-only.
